PullRequest.Title: Keep the chat's custom agent when a queued message starts
PullRequest.Body:

Refs #341837

## Problem

In an Agent Host chat with a custom agent selected, a message you queue while a turn is running starts without that agent. The agent picker still shows the custom agent, but the queued turn runs with the default agent, and the provider drops its custom agent selection until the next direct send. Messages another session sends with `send_message` have the same problem. The issue's comment reports this ("agent definition should be loaded in queue also").

## Root cause

Model and agent selection travel on each turn's message. Before a turn is sent, the host applies the message's agent with `changeAgent(chat, message.agent)` ([agentSideEffects.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentSideEffects.ts#L2235)). The protocol defines a message without `agent` as "no custom agent, the provider's default behavior applies" ([state.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-chat/state.ts#L872-L878)). The Copilot, Claude and Codex providers all clear their custom agent when they get `undefined`.

Direct sends set `agent` from the selected mode ([agentHostSessionHandler.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts#L3704)), but the pending messages the workbench publishes for queued and steering requests never did ([agentHostSessionHandler.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts#L2522-L2529)). The `send_message` tool builds its queued, steering and started messages without an agent too ([sessionServerTools.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/sessionServerTools.ts#L1625-L1656), [agentService.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L2585-L2593)). So when such a message started a turn, the host switched the chat to the default agent. A side effect in the workbench: the next local change to the queue re-published a message queued elsewhere without its agent.

## Fix

The messages now say which agent they run with, as the protocol expects, and the host's `changeAgent` handling is unchanged:

- **Workbench:** a pending message carries the custom agent that was selected when it was queued, read from the request's mode the same way a direct send does (shared helper `getRequestedAgentUri`). A pending message that came from the host has no local mode, so it keeps the agent it already has instead of being re-published without one.
- **Host, `send_message`:** queued, steering and directly started messages carry the target chat's current agent, which is the agent of its latest turn (new helper `getLatestTurnAgent`). New chats have no turns, so `create_session` and `create_chat` prompts are unchanged.

A host-side "skip `changeAgent` when the message has no agent" guard would be wrong: a direct send without an agent is how you switch back to the default agent. That still works, and a unit test now covers it. Other turns the host writes itself, such as agent merge prompts, still carry no agent; they are left for a separate change.

## Before / after

Agents window connected to a mock agent host that offers a "Reviewer" custom agent. Every reply starts with the agent the host selected for that turn. Reviewer is selected, "Review the parser" keeps running, and "Then summarize the changes" is queued.

### Before

![Before: the queued message replies "Agent: default" while the picker still shows Reviewer](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/2e0384c1a242e5766de38531c4c4db751e150dc8/20261015-171820-C15-F1/before.gif?raw=true)

### After

![After: the queued message replies "Agent: Reviewer"](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/2e0384c1a242e5766de38531c4c4db751e150dc8/20261015-171820-C15-F1/after.gif?raw=true)

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a Copilot chat on the Agent Host and pick a custom agent in the agent picker.
2. Send a prompt that takes a while, then type a second message and add it to the queue (set `chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction` to `queue` to make Enter queue).
3. When the first turn ends and the queued message starts, it runs with the custom agent. The automated repro below shows this with a mock agent that reports which agent the host selected for each turn.
4. Pick the built-in Agent mode and send: the chat switches back to the default agent.

<details><summary>Automated repro (mock agent host + Agents window)</summary>

The repro uses the scripted mock agent from `out/`, so it needs no account. Save the three files next to each other, build (`npm run transpile-client`), then:

1. `node runHost.cjs` with `BS_VSCODE` set to the checkout root (starts the host on `ws://127.0.0.1:8985`).
2. Launch the Agents window (`.agents/skills/launch`) with `--agents --disable-extension GitHub.copilot-chat`, and set `chat.remoteAgentHosts` to `[{ "address": "ws://127.0.0.1:8985", "name": "Mock Host" }]`, `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable: true` and `chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction: "queue"`.
3. `node <bug-swarm skill>/scripts/cdp-scenario.mjs --cdp <port> --scenario repro.cjs --out <dir>` (fails on main, passes with this PR).

`repro.cjs`:

```js
// Repro: a message queued while a turn runs must start with the custom agent the chat had selected.
// Runs over CDP against an Agents window connected to the mock Agent Host in mockhost.mjs (chat.remoteAgentHosts).
// The mock agent starts every reply with "Agent: <name>", the agent the host selected for that turn, and writes the
// host's agent changes to BS_STATUS, which is reported as an independent check.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os = require('os');

const PROMPT = 'Review the parser';
const QUEUED = 'Then summarize the changes';
const STATUS = process.env.BS_STATUS || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-agent-host-status.json');
const readStatus = () => { try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(STATUS, 'utf8')); } catch { return { agentChanges: [], turns: [] }; } };

let turnCount = 0;

async function waitFor(fn, timeoutMs, intervalMs = 100) {
	const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
	let value;
	while (Date.now() < end) {
		value = await fn();
		if (value) { return value; }
		await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
	}
	return value;
}

// This repro needs no Copilot account: dismiss the sign-in prompt, which can open a few seconds after the window starts.
async function dismissSignIn(page) {
	for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
		const cont = page.getByText('Continue Without Signing In');
		if (await cont.count()) { await cont.first().click(); await page.waitForTimeout(800); continue; }
		if (!await page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.monaco-dialog-box, .monaco-dialog-modal-block, .sessions-signing-in-dialog-modal-block'))) { break; }
		await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
		await page.waitForTimeout(800);
	}
}

const replies = page => page.evaluate(() => {
	const down = [...document.querySelectorAll('.chat-scroll-down')].find(e => e.offsetParent);
	down?.click();
	return [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-response')].filter(e => e.offsetParent).map(e => [...e.querySelectorAll('.rendered-markdown')].map(m => m.textContent).join(' ').trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' '));
});
const pendingRows = page => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-item-container.pending-request')]
	.filter(e => e.offsetParent)
	.map(e => (e.querySelector('.value')?.textContent ?? e.textContent).trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ')));
const pickerLabel = page => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-input-part .action-label')]
	.filter(e => e.offsetParent && (e.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Pick Mode')).at(-1)?.textContent.trim());

module.exports = {
	id: 'queued-message-keeps-custom-agent',
	title: 'A queued message starts with the chat\'s custom agent',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341837',
	stepPauseMs: 1500,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'open', title: 'Open a session on the mock agent host', async run({ page }) {
				await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row')].some(r => (r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Agent mock')), null, { timeout: 60000 });
				await dismissSignIn(page);
				const rowId = await page.evaluate(() => {
					const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row')].filter(r => r.offsetParent);
					const header = rows.findIndex(r => (r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Agent mock'));
					return rows.slice(header + 1).find(r => /^(Parser review|Session),/.test(r.getAttribute('aria-label') || ''))?.id;
				});
				if (!rowId) { throw new Error('The mock host session is not in the sessions list'); }
				await page.locator(`[id="${rowId}"]`).click();
				await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-request')].some(e => e.textContent.includes('Look at the parser module') || e.textContent.includes('Review the parser')), null, { timeout: 30000 });
				return 'The session transcript is visible';
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'pick', title: 'Select the Reviewer custom agent', async run({ page }) {
				await dismissSignIn(page);
				await page.locator('.interactive-input-part .action-label[aria-label^="Pick Mode"]:visible').last().click();
				await page.getByRole('option', { name: 'Reviewer', exact: true }).click();
				const label = await waitFor(async () => (await pickerLabel(page)) === 'Reviewer' && 'Reviewer', 5000);
				if (!label) { throw new Error(`The agent picker shows "${await pickerLabel(page)}"`); }
				return 'The agent picker shows Reviewer';
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'send', title: `Send "${PROMPT}"; the turn keeps running`, async run({ page }) {
				turnCount = readStatus().turns.length;
				const input = page.locator('.interactive-input-part .monaco-editor:visible').last();
				await input.click();
				await page.keyboard.type(PROMPT, { delay: 15 });
				await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
				const reply = await waitFor(async () => readStatus().turns.length > turnCount && (await replies(page)).at(-1)?.includes('Reviewing the parser') && (await replies(page)).at(-1), 30000);
				if (!reply) { throw new Error('The turn did not start'); }
				return `Reply so far: "${reply}"`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'queue', title: `Queue "${QUEUED}" while the turn runs`, async run({ page }) {
				const input = page.locator('.interactive-input-part .monaco-editor:visible').last();
				await input.click();
				await page.keyboard.type(QUEUED, { delay: 15 });
				await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
				const rows = await waitFor(async () => { const r = await pendingRows(page); return r.some(t => t.includes(QUEUED)) && r; }, 10000);
				if (!rows) { throw new Error(`The message was not queued; pending rows: ${JSON.stringify(await pendingRows(page))}`); }
				return `Queued: ${JSON.stringify(rows)}`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'drain', title: 'The first turn ends and the queued message starts', async run({ page }) {
				const reply = await waitFor(async () => readStatus().turns.slice(turnCount).some(t => t.prompt === QUEUED) && (await replies(page)).at(-1)?.includes('Summary:') && (await replies(page)).at(-1), 40000);
				if (!reply) { throw new Error('The queued message did not start'); }
				return `Queued message reply: "${reply}"`;
			}
		},
		{
			id: 'check', title: 'The queued message ran with the Reviewer agent', async run({ page }) {
				const reply = (await replies(page)).findLast(t => t.includes('Summary:'));
				const hostTurn = readStatus().turns.slice(turnCount).find(t => t.prompt === QUEUED);
				const picker = await pickerLabel(page);
				const agent = /Agent: (\w+)\./.exec(reply)?.[1];
				if (agent !== 'Reviewer') {
					throw new Error(`The queued message ran with the ${agent} agent instead of Reviewer. Reply: "${reply}"; host selected: ${hostTurn?.agent}; picker shows: ${picker}`);
				}
				return `Reply: "${reply}"; host selected: ${hostTurn?.agent}; picker shows: ${picker}`;
			}
		},
	]
};
```

`mockhost.mjs`:

```js
// Standalone Agent Host (from a built VS Code checkout's out/) with the ScriptedMockAgent, used to show which custom
// agent a queued message runs with.
// - Seeds one session mock:/bs-agent titled "Parser review" with a one-turn history.
// - Publishes one custom agent, "Reviewer", in the session's customizations so the chat's agent picker offers it.
// - Records every changeAgent call the host makes and writes it to BS_STATUS (JSON).
// - Every reply starts with "Agent: <name>", the agent the host selected for that turn ("Reviewer" or "default").
// - A prompt starting with "Review the parser" keeps its turn running for BS_HOLD_MS (default 15000 ms).
// Usage (from an interactive terminal: the server exits when stdin closes): node runHost.cjs
//   env BS_VSCODE = checkout root, BS_PORT, BS_UDD, BS_STATUS, BS_HOLD_MS
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import path from 'node:path';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';

const VSCODE = process.env.BS_VSCODE || process.cwd();
const out = p => pathToFileURL(path.join(VSCODE, 'out', p)).href;
const HOLD_MS = Number(process.env.BS_HOLD_MS || 15000);
const STATUS = process.env.BS_STATUS || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-agent-host-status.json');
const SESSION = 'mock:/bs-agent';
const TITLE = 'Parser review';
const REVIEWER_URI = 'file:///bs-agents/reviewer.agent.md';
process.env.VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_MOCK_SEED_SESSIONS = SESSION;

const mock = await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/mockAgent.js'));
const fx = await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/historyRecordFixtures.js'));
const { URI } = await import(out('vs/base/common/uri.js'));

const status = { pid: process.pid, agentChanges: [], turns: [] };
const writeStatus = () => fs.writeFileSync(STATUS, JSON.stringify(status, null, 1));
writeStatus();
const logLine = s => process.stderr.write(`[bs-agent] ${s}\n`);

let currentAgentUri;
const agentName = () => currentAgentUri === REVIEWER_URI ? 'Reviewer' : currentAgentUri ? currentAgentUri : 'default';

const P = mock.ScriptedMockAgent.prototype;
P.getChatCustomizations = async function () {
	return [{
		type: 'directory', id: 'bs-agents', uri: 'file:///bs-agents', name: 'Agents',
		enabled: true, contents: 'agent', writable: false,
		children: [{ type: 'agent', id: 'reviewer', uri: REVIEWER_URI, name: 'Reviewer', description: 'Reviews code changes' }],
	}];
};

let history;
const origGet = P.getSessionMessages;
P.getSessionMessages = async function (session) {
	const s = decodeURIComponent(session.toString());
	if (s.includes('bs-agent') && !s.includes('subagent')) {
		history ??= fx.buildTurnsFromHistory([
			{ type: 'message', role: 'user', session: URI.parse(SESSION), messageId: 'u-0', content: 'Look at the parser module.' },
			{ type: 'message', role: 'assistant', session: URI.parse(SESSION), messageId: 'a-0', content: 'Ready. The parser lives in src/parser.ts.' },
		]);
		return history;
	}
	return origGet.call(this, session);
};
const label = s => String(s).includes('bs-agent') ? TITLE : undefined;
const origFireDisc = P.fireDiscoveredChats;
P.fireDiscoveredChats = function (chats) {
	return origFireDisc.call(this, chats.map(m => ({ ...m, external: false, summary: label(m.session) ?? m.summary })));
};
for (const k of ['listExternalChats', 'listSessions']) {
	const o = P[k];
	P[k] = async function (...a) { return (await o.apply(this, a)).map(m => ({ ...m, summary: label(m.session) ?? m.summary })); };
}
for (const k of ['getSessionMetadata', 'getChatMetadata']) {
	const o = P[k];
	P[k] = async function (...a) { const r = await o.apply(this, a); const l = label(String(a[1]?.toString?.() ?? '') + String(a[0])); return r && l ? { ...r, summary: l } : r; };
}
const origDesc = P.getDescriptor;
P.getDescriptor = function () {
	if (!this.__bsInit) {
		this.__bsInit = true;
		const origChange = this.chats.changeAgent;
		this.chats.changeAgent = (chat, agent, context) => {
			currentAgentUri = agent?.uri;
			status.agentChanges.push({ at: Date.now(), chat: chat.toString(), agent: agent?.uri ?? null });
			writeStatus();
			logLine(`changeAgent ${agent?.uri ?? '(default)'}`);
			return origChange(chat, agent, context);
		};
		for (const ms of [1500, 5000]) {
			setTimeout(() => {
				void this.listExternalChats().then(chats => { this.fireDiscoveredChats(chats); });
			}, ms);
		}
		for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
			setTimeout(() => {
				try {
					this._onDidChatProgress.fire({ kind: 'action', resource: URI.parse(SESSION), action: { type: 'session/titleChanged', title: TITLE } });
				} catch (e) { logLine(`title failed: ${e}`); }
			}, 2000 + i * 3000);
		}
	}
	return origDesc.call(this);
};

const origFire = P._fireSequence;
P._fireSequence = function (signals) {
	const first = signals[0];
	const content = first?.action?.part && typeof first.action.part.content === 'string' ? first.action.part.content : '';
	const match = /^Unknown prompt: (.*)$/s.exec(content);
	if (!match) {
		return origFire.call(this, signals);
	}
	const prompt = match[1];
	const agent = agentName();
	const turn = { turnId: first.action.turnId, prompt, agent, startedAt: Date.now() };
	status.turns.push(turn);
	writeStatus();
	logLine(`turn "${prompt}" agent=${agent}`);
	const hold = /^Review the parser/.test(prompt);
	const text = `Agent: ${agent}. ${hold ? 'Reviewing the parser, this takes a while…' : 'Summary: the parser changes look good.'}`;
	const reply = { ...first, action: { ...first.action, part: { ...first.action.part, content: text } } };
	if (!hold) {
		return origFire.call(this, [reply, ...signals.slice(1)]);
	}
	this._onDidChatProgress.fire(reply);
	setTimeout(() => {
		turn.completedAt = Date.now();
		writeStatus();
		this._onDidChatProgress.fire(signals[signals.length - 1]);
	}, HOLD_MS);
};

process.argv = [process.argv[0], process.argv[1], '--enable-mock-agent', '--port', process.env.BS_PORT || '8985', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--without-connection-token', '--quiet', '--user-data-dir', process.env.BS_UDD || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-agent-ahost-udd')];
await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostServerMain.js'));
setInterval(() => { }, 1 << 30);
```

<sub>Found and fixed with automated exploratory testing. Draft until reviewed by a human.</sub>

Scenarios.Scenario: An agent invokes send_message for a target chat that is busy, causing the message to be queued or used as steering input and later drained into a provider turn.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The tool resolves sessions and the target chat, reads in-memory target state, then dispatches one pending-message action; queue delivery later admits one turn and reaches working-directory/checkpoint setup, agent selection, and provider send. The added latest-agent lookup and message field are constant-time and do not add a blocking step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate session metadata through AgentService.listSessions, which may read persisted session registry/state and coalesces concurrent list computations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical listSessions request per send_message invocation, with same-mode concurrent computations coalesced by registry epoch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The send_message path already awaited the same listSessions operation before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before resolving the target session and chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast/transport the ChatPendingMessageSet state action to subscribed clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action for the logical queued or steering message; the added agent selection only adds a small URI field to that existing payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same pending-message action crossed the protocol boundary, without the agent field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The server-side action is dispatched before the tool reports queued/steered; client transport follows the existing state propagation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve working directory and capture the turn-start checkpoint when the queued message is eventually drained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for the drained turn; target-chat queue admission allows one active turn at a time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Queue drain already performed the same setup for every queued turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Checkpoint and selection setup complete before provider message send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply agent selection and send the drained turn to the agent provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One changeAgent call and one provider turn send per admitted message; carrying the existing custom selection changes the argument, not call count or concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same changeAgent boundary was called with undefined and the same provider turn was sent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider selection is awaited before the turn is sent.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One target chat per tool invocation; cost of retained agent metadata grows linearly with queued-message count by one small selection object/URI per message, while provider and protocol boundary cardinality remains one per logical message.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tool invocations remain subject to the existing orchestration message limiter. Messages for a busy target are retained in its queue and drained through the existing single-active-turn admission path rather than fanned out by this change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The latest-agent value comes from in-memory chat state. Session listing has existing in-flight coalescing by external-session mode and registry epoch; the change neither changes cache keys nor cold/warm behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines add only an O(1) latest-turn lookup and a field on the already-created action, while traced action and provider boundaries retain their prior cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent URI length and unusually large queue depths vary, but the added bytes and allocations are bounded per existing queued message and are not substantial enough to establish a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new boundary, fan-out, concurrency burst, or repeated provider work is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: An agent invokes send_message for an idle target chat, so the host starts the turn immediately.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing session-list lookup and argument resolution, the changed code reads the latest turn agent from in-memory state, builds the message, and enters the existing turn admission/provider-send path. The added work is O(1) before the same expensive provider workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate/merge known session metadata for target resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per send_message, with existing in-flight coalescing for concurrent listings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical session listing occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks target resolution before the immediate turn can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the working directory and capture a turn-start checkpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The immediate turn path already performed these operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Working-directory resolution and checkpoint completion precede provider send.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Change the provider's selected agent and send the prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One changeAgent call and one send per turn, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same call count occurred, but changeAgent received undefined rather than the custom selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Agent selection is awaited on the provider-send critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time array tail access and one small message field per immediate send; history length does not affect `turns.at(-1)`.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrency is added: the turn uses existing per-chat admission, selection Promise.all, and provider scheduling. The diff does not launch additional promises.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The agent selection is read directly from current in-memory chat state with no cache or miss behavior. Existing session-list coalescing remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete path shows unchanged expensive operations and unchanged boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and checkpoint duration varies, but none of that cost is introduced or amplified by these lines.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the change preserves selection metadata without adding I/O, latency-bearing awaits, or duplicate provider calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user queues, steers, reorders, or removes pending requests in an Agent Host chat, causing renderer-side pending-message synchronization.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each explicit pending-queue mutation synchronously rebuilds snapshots for the current queue and deep-compares them with protocol state; changed custom-agent requests additionally decode/normalize their wrapped URI. Only new or changed snapshots dispatch protocol actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Decode agent-host URI metadata (URL query parsing, base64/JSON decode) and stringify the original URI for custom-mode pending requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per pending request with custom mode instructions on each pending-queue change event; default-agent and host-origin requests skip decoding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pending synchronization already traversed the full queue but did not decode the selected-agent URI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously inside the queue-change callback before diff dispatch, but alongside pre-existing per-item attachment conversion, model selection, maps, and deep comparisons.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and send ChatPendingMessageSet/Removed/Reordered notifications to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One set action per actually new or changed message, plus existing removal/reorder actions; deep equality includes the agent URI and suppresses unchanged snapshots despite fresh wrapper objects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same logical pending mutations dispatched the same action count, with a slightly smaller payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notifications are emitted after local snapshot construction; no response is awaited by the synchronous callback.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with effective pending-queue length Q per explicit mutation. The newly added URI decode is O(Q) only for custom-mode entries; queues are user-created message queues and the existing synchronization already performs materially larger O(Q) snapshot/attachment/equality work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The model event callback is synchronous and processes the queue serially. Protocol sends remain one-way notifications; this change does not use Promise.all or create parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used for URI conversion. Protocol-state comparison acts as deduplication, so unchanged entries do not generate repeat IPC; remote projections are guarded to avoid feedback synchronization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener registration, full-loop placement, URI decoder implementation, deep equality, and dispatch boundary were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large manually accumulated queues would increase synchronous decode work, but realistic queue cardinality and tiny URI metadata make the incremental cost insufficient for a high-confidence user-visible regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the only new scaling CPU work is a small URI normalization per custom queued request, with no added IPC cardinality or hot render/frame trigger.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and traced server-tool delivery, immediate and queued provider startup, renderer pending synchronization, protocol transport, state access, persistence/session listing, and provider boundaries. The PR adds constant-time state lookup and bounded metadata propagation; it does not introduce a concrete actionable performance regression or a qualifying shipped-regression fix.
